claims.text: Spotify's Honk verifiers activate automatically based on repository contents, are exposed to the agent via MCP, and use regexes to surface only the most relevant errors.
Spotify's LLM judge vetoes about a quarter of agent sessions, and the agent course-corrects about half the time after a veto; scope creep is the most common trigger.
Spotify runs its verifiers in Claude Code's stop hook; if any verifier fails, no PR is opened.
Spotify reports 1,500+ agent-generated PRs merged into production and 60-90% time savings on migrations.
Ramp's Inspect runs each session in a Modal Sandbox with Postgres, Redis, Temporal and RabbitMQ, started from filesystem snapshots rebuilt every 30 minutes.
Ramp's Inspect starts about half of Ramp's merged PRs, and over 80% of Inspect's own code is written by Inspect.
Meta's RADAR reviewed 535K+ diffs and landed 331K+, peaking at around 25K diffs per day.
Meta's RACER runbooks must show a 60-day clean track record, daily caps, DRS thresholds and a denylist before being onboarded to RADAR auto-landing.
Uber's Shepherd migrated about 75,000 JUnit test classes (1.25M lines of code) in four months via 5,000+ diffs, using AI only to debug failures.
Google's LLM migration study covered 39 migrations by three developers over twelve months; 74.45% of 595 code changes were LLM-generated, with an estimated 50% reduction in time.
